rationale:
ROUND 4 on dc62975f. Round 3 was APPROVED (2 advisories, none high). I am resubmitting anyway, because acting on one of those advisories REVERSED a design decision the previous two rounds argued over, and a Council-Reviewed trailer must describe the code that exists.

THE REVERSAL. bug_historian's medium advisory: with escalate_chrome_store_failure OFF, a slot with NOTHING EVER STORED that the new UTF-8 gate refuses does not fail the build — and bugs_closed/054 already ruled that filing an item without failing the step is insufficient escalation for an unserved chrome slot. Checking that sent me back to my own caller, and the reading is worse than the advisory says: THE ARM COULD NEVER GATE 'STORE FAILURES' AT ALL. Escalation is reached only through chromeUnserved, which is appended to only when !chromeSlotHasStoredHTML. So the one and only thing my opt-in key gated was A SLOT WITH NOTHING TO SERVE — precisely the state bugs_open/260 and bugs_closed/054 already ruled must fail, greenfield builds explicitly included. Round 2's gate withheld an approved protection from the only case it was written for.

AND THE ENUMERATION THE GUARDIAN ASKED FOR FINISHES THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE GATE RATHER THAN FOR IT. Round 2 reasoned from '7 workflows, none with an error_step' to 'therefore default OFF'. That was the right query and the wrong population: the seven-workflow figure bounds who is affected WHEN the arm fires, and I never measured HOW OFTEN it can fire. MEASURED 2026-09-02: across the entire fleet, exactly ONE site_components row has NULL or empty rendered_html — garden-tools.uk's footer — and this change repairs it at source. A site with no chrome ROW at all takes the 'no row matched' path instead, which is bugs_open/435 and still silent. So the gate protected seven pipelines from a population of one.

SO THE KEY AND ITS SENTINEL ARE DELETED, not left inert, and a store refusal now takes bugs_open/260's existing reviewed disposition unchanged. This is strictly less new machinery than round 3: no chromeStoreRefusedError, no escalate_chrome_store_failure, no errors.As, no new config surface. It also dissolves four of the round-3 advisories rather than deferring them — guardian's 'undeclared key fails open silently on a typo', architecture's 'the key is invisible to the RFC_022 counter', architecture's 'nothing integration-tests the armed path', and bug_historian's own — because the key no longer exists. A flag whose measured population is one row, which withholds a ruled-on protection, and which nothing declares, is not caution; it is a mechanism rotting unexercised, which this estate has been bitten by before.

I want to be explicit that two seats moved me in opposite directions and I am not simply obeying the more recent one. Guardian (round 1, HIGH) was right that I asserted a blast radius instead of enumerating it. bug_historian (round 3) was right that the remedy I chose withheld an approved protection. Both are satisfied by the same answer, and it is the MEASUREMENT that decides between them, not the seniority of the objection: the enumeration guardian demanded is what shows the escalation is nearly inert, and an escalation that is nearly inert has no need of a flag. If a seat still disagrees, the disagreement is now about a number that can be re-run in one query, which is the state I would want it in.

edits.symbol: UpperFirst + InvalidUTF8At (and this file's own converted call site)
edits.rationale:
The primitive. Upper-cases the FIRST RUNE, leaves the rest byte-identical, and returns already-invalid input untouched rather than substituting U+FFFD — this helper's job is not to CREATE the defect, and silently rewriting a caller's bad bytes would hide one a validator upstream should be naming. Placed beside SafeCut/TruncateString because they are the same class and a reader looking for one should find the other.

SAME FILE, also: InvalidUTF8At — The diagnostic Postgres does not give. Returns the byte offset of the first invalid sequence and a QuoteToASCII'd window (±48 bytes) around it. ASCII-only is deliberate and load-bearing: the report is logged, persisted and put in a work item summary, so a window carrying the raw bad bytes would reproduce the very defect it describes — which is precisely what the third edit below is about.

And this file's own instance of the idiom (:1980, in the display-name splitter) converted to UpperFirst, like the other seven.

edits.symbol: the live defect (:1622), half 1, the pre-store UTF-8 gate, the 3 truncations, the emitter phase — and the REMOVAL of round 2's escalation gate

What remains is: the byte-slice fix at the defect site; a store failure that returns its error instead of nil and files through the SAME emitter bugs_closed/054's lineage produced; a pre-store UTF-8 gate that refuses with a byte OFFSET Postgres will not give; three rune-safe truncations; and an honest `phase` on the emitter. The pre-existing execution-failure call site is updated for the widened signature and is shown below (editquality round 3, medium).

edits.symbol: the 8th call site (:411) — shown, not asserted
edits.rationale: Round 1 named this file in prose and gave no diff, and editquality was right to refuse that: either it is a real edit and belongs in the submission, or the class-fix claim is false. It is a real edit. It is the only one of the eight needing an added import, which is itself worth a reviewer seeing. Its risk is the lowest of the eight — a one-shot harvesting CLI, not a live path — but 'low risk' was never the reason to omit it; the 8-edit budget was, and that is a bookkeeping excuse for an unverifiable claim.

Two of the eight call sites, both deriving a site's LOGO TEXT from a name. Same byte slice, same failure: a company name beginning with a non-ASCII letter (an accented capital, a curly quote) is corrupted, and logo text is written to config and rendered into chrome — i.e. straight back at Postgres. Converted, not merely noted: leaving a known member of the class unfixed because it has not bitten yet is how the 2026-07-20 truncation fix missed the casing shape for six weeks.
The third logo-text derivation, in the render path itself. Same conversion, same reason as multipage_actions.go.
Call site 5 of 8. Converted in the same pass so the census can be re-run and come back clean.

Call site 6 of 8. HumaniseKey turns snake_case into a label; keys are ASCII today, so this one is a latent member rather than a live one — converted anyway, because the value of a class fix is that the next reader does not have to re-derive which members were safe. The eighth site, cmd/webdesignport/harvest.go:411, is converted identically and needed only an added datahelpers import; it is outside council scope so it has no edit of its own here.

Round 3's three escalation-gate tests are DELETED with the gate; the claim about them is withdrawn rather than illustrated (editquality round 3, low). Stated plainly: five tests in total across this change, and half 1's two dispositions are verified at the ARTEFACT after the roll rather than by unit test, because reaching them requires mocking the entire render path. The deleted tests never covered them either, so no coverage is lost by the removal.

plan.risks:
THE ROUND-2 RISK IS WITHDRAWN BY DELETION, and replaced by the round-1 one in its true size. A store refusal on a slot with NOTHING to serve now fails the step, ungated. Measured population: ONE row fleet-wide (garden-tools.uk's footer), which this change repairs at source — so the expected number of newly-failing builds is zero, and the residual case is a greenfield build whose chrome cannot be stored, which bugs_open/260 states it WANTS to fail.

What I cannot measure is future greenfield volume. If many new sites are built and something upstream starts producing invalid UTF-8, this fails those builds loudly rather than shipping footerless sites quietly. I hold that is the intended behaviour and it is 260's, not a new authority — but it is the sharp edge of this change and it is no longer behind a flag.

Half 1's two dispositions are not unit-tested (reaching them needs the whole render path mocked); they are verified at the artefact after the roll. Deploy verification: ask the pod for 'build provenance', and because that line scrolls, fall back to a binary probe carrying BOTH a must-be-present and a must-be-absent control — never a bare strings|grep, never git, never the tag.

The gate REFUSES invalid UTF-8 rather than sanitising; a producer needing lossy repair should get it at the producer, and this gate is what will name the producer.

The 8-site conversion is behaviour-preserving only on ASCII, pinned by test; on non-ASCII it changes corrupt to correct, and no consumer of the corrupt form can exist because such a string could not round-trip through Postgres.

:1411 remains silent by a measured decision and is now FILED as bugs_open/435 rather than left as a comment.

Go, so inert until the next chassis roll. gofmt reports the file unformatted at HEAD from another lane's commit (effc3a090), not from this change; left alone so a gofmt -w does not sweep their line into this commit.
